title: Tracheostomy care at home
what: A tracheostomy is an opening in the neck through which a person breathes via a tube. At home it needs care every day to keep the tube clean and the skin healthy.
why: When a person cannot breathe normally through the mouth and nose and the doctor placed a tracheostomy for the long term.
duration: care usually takes 15 to 30 minutes once or twice a day; suctioning as needed
tell_doctor: If there is more mucus, or it changed color or smell
If the skin around the opening is red, weeping or bleeding
If the tube is hard to insert or keeps shifting
If you are short of supplies or not sure of your skills

prepare.title: Training
prepare.text: Before discharge, ask the nurse to show you everything and do the care yourself a few times with her.

prepare.title: Spare tube
prepare.text: Always keep a spare tube of the same size and one size smaller within reach.

prepare.title: Equipment
prepare.text: Suction machine, catheters, wipes, boiled water, split gauze pads, ties.

prepare.title: Air
prepare.text: Dry air dries out mucus. A humidifier in the room is usually advised.

bring: Discharge papers and the doctor's contact
A list of questions for the doctor
steps: Wash your hands and put on gloves
If you hear gurgling, suction the mucus with a catheter as you were taught
Take out the inner tube, if there is one, and rinse it
Remove the old gauze and look at the skin
Wipe the skin around the opening with a damp wipe and pat dry
Put a new split gauze under the tube
Change the ties: hold the tube with your hand until the old ones are replaced
One finger should fit between the tie and the neck
feel: Suctioning causes coughing. This is normal
The person may be frightened. Speak calmly and explain each step
after: Watch the color and amount of mucus
Keep water from getting into the tube when washing
The whole tube is replaced on the doctor's schedule
Keep the emergency number where you can see it
red_flags: The tube came out or is blocked and cannot be cleared: insert the spare and call your local emergency number
The person is gasping and the lips turn blue: call your local emergency number
More than a few streaks of blood from the tube: call your local emergency number
Fever, thick yellow or green mucus with a smell: see a doctor

faq.q: Can a person with a tracheostomy speak?
faq.a: Sometimes, with a special valve. The doctor decides whether it is possible in your case.

faq.q: How often should mucus be suctioned?
faq.a: As needed, when you hear gurgling or the person cannot cough it up. Not by the clock.

reminders.text: Morning tracheostomy care: hands, gloves, suction, gauze, ties. Spare tube within reach.
